title: AFFAIRE FOGARASI ET AUTRES c. ROUMANIE
conclusion: Violation de l'article 3 - Interdiction de la torture (Article 3 - Traitement dégradant;Traitement inhumain) (Volet matériel);Violation de l'article 3 - Interdiction de la torture (Article 3 - Enquête effective) (Volet procédural)
summary: In Fogarasi and Others v. Romania, the applicants—a family of four, all members of the Roma community—brought a case against Romania concerning police violence and the lack of an effective investigation. The case focused on the vulnerability of Roma and Travellers to police abuse and the failure of authorities to protect them from inhuman and degrading treatment. On 4 July 2008, following a neighbourhood dispute in Acîş, police were called to the applicants’ home. After an initial visit, officers returned with reinforcements, leading to a confrontation in which the first applicant was struck on the head by a neighbour while police looked on. Later, special police forces arrived at the local dispensary, where the family had sought medical help, and forcibly detained the applicants—including their 13-year-old daughter—subjecting them to physical violence both en route to and inside the police station. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which prohibits torture and inhuman or degrading treatment. The Court found that the first three applicants had suffered such treatment at the hands of the police and that the authorities failed to conduct an effective investigation, thus violating both the substantive and procedural limbs of Article 3. This judgment is significant as it highlights the persistent risks of police brutality and impunity faced by Roma and Travellers in Europe, reflecting a broader historical pattern of discrimination and neglect.
